title: Movie Secrets From 'The Mandalorian and Grogu'
summary:
Hal Hickel works at Industrial Light & Magic, or ILM, a company that makes movie special effects. On Thursday, at the View Conference in Turin, Italy, he shared secrets from "The Mandalorian and Grogu."

Hickel kept asking, "What would Phil do?" He meant Phil Tippett, an expert in stop-motion. In stop-motion, puppets are moved a tiny bit at a time and photographed frame by frame. Tippett worked on the first "Star Wars" movies.

The team made the giant AT-AT walkers move slowly to show how heavy they are. For a smaller walker, animators studied ostriches.

Rotta the Hutt is voiced by Jeremy Allen White. Director Jon Favreau felt the first design "didn't feel Hutt-y enough," so the team made Rotta look more like his father, Jabba. Rotta speaks English so younger viewers do not have to read lots of subtitles.

The movie even has a real stop-motion fight between two giant droids. Hickel moved a puppet himself!
why_it_matters: It shows kids that movie magic often comes from real puppets and hard work, not just computers.
